claims.explanation: Hydroxyfasudil is a ROCK inhibitor whose selectivity in this screen tracks with PTEN loss and PI3K/AKT pathway activation: PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among the most killed, consistent with ROCK inhibition amplifying PI3K/AKT-dependent signaling and dependence. Conversely, RAS/BRAF-mutant lines with intact PTEN (e.g., NCIH1299, K029AX, SH4, LOXIMVI) are relatively protected, suggesting MAPK-driven lines do not require ROCK activity for survival.

features.basis: PTEN loss enriched in killed lines; PI3K/AKT activation may synergize with ROCK inhibition
PIK3CA-mutant lines (MKN1, HCC1954) appear in killed set, consistent with PI3K pathway dependence
TP53 mutation is highly prevalent among killed lines, though common across all lines
KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1299, HS766T, PATU8988S) are enriched in least-affected set
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (K029AX, SH4, LOXIMVI) are relatively protected
NF1-mutant lines appear in both sets but RAS-pathway activation may reduce ROCK dependence
Hydroxyfasudil targets ROCK1; higher expression may increase dependence on ROCK signaling
ROCK2 is the closely related Rho-kinase isoform inhibited by hydroxyfasudil
Hydroxyfasudil increases eNOS expression; high baseline eNOS may buffer against cytotoxicity
ROCK inhibition activates PI3K/AKT; high AKT may increase dependence on this survival pathway
ARID1A mutations appear more frequently in least-affected lines (SNUC5, HS766T, LOXIMVI)
CDKN2A loss appears in several killed lines (KELLY, SUIT2) but also protected lines
